title: Short Stuff: Teresita Basa
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1980s-era murder of Teresita Basa, a Filipino respiratory therapist found dead in her Chicago apartment fire. Six months later, a trance claim by co-worker Remy Chiwa (wife of Dr. Joe Chiwa) named Alan Showery as the killer and described stolen jewelry; detectives verified the jewelry and Showery was arrested, confessed, and was later convicted. A judge upheld the arrest despite the trance-based tip. The hosts also briefly note Edgewater Hospital's history and discuss the case's place in American law enforcement.

segments.title: Opening banter on Chicago and Edgewater Hospital
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Chicago feeling haunted and mention Edgewater Hospital, where Hillary Clinton and John Wayne Gacy were reportedly born, and introduce the Teresita Basa story.

segments.title: Murder of Teresita Basa
segments.summary: Basa, a 47-year-old Filipino respiratory therapist at Edgewater Hospital, is found dead in her Chicago apartment fire on February 2 with a kitchen knife in her chest. Detectives run out of leads after about six months.

segments.title: Trance tip from Remy Chiwa
segments.summary: About six months later, Detective Joe Statuela gets a referral from Evanston police to Dr. Joe Chiwa in Skokie. Chiwa says his wife went into trances in Tagalog claiming to be Basa, naming her killer and stolen jewelry, and gave names and phone numbers of people who could identify the jewelry.

segments.title: Verification and arrest of Alan Showery
segments.summary: Police check the tip: Alan Showery had worked with Basa, and he voluntarily came to the station, initially claimed he went to fix a TV but was called off, and eventually admitted going to the apartment. His girlfriend had jewelry he said was a late Christmas present, and Basa's relatives identified it. Showery was arrested.

segments.title: Court ruling on trance-based arrest and conviction
segments.summary: Defense attorney William Swanno argued the arrest lacked probable cause and rested on a trance. The judge upheld the arrest, saying police had to check the tip. Showery later pleaded guilty during a retrial wait and received a long sentence for murder, robbery and arson, serving about five years.

segments.title: Wrap-up and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts discuss possible explanations, including that Chiwa knew Basa and Showery and may have been afraid to come forward, and sign off.
